criteria.criterion: A new plan.rs unit test shows two entries that touch disjoint code files plus the same CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md land in one parallel group; run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`.
criteria.evidence: New test `shared_append_only_files_are_not_a_clash_but_other_shared_paths_and_lone_shared_entries_are` builds "one" (crates/a/src/lib.rs + CHANGELOG.md + docs/decisions.md) and "two" (crates/b/src/lib.rs + the same two files) and asserts they share a group. Under the old `disjoint` they would clash on CHANGELOG.md, so the test fails without the fix. All 11 plan tests passed.

criteria.criterion: A test shows two entries that both touch the same non-shared file (e.g. crates/core/src/x.rs) still land in separate groups, and an entry touching only CHANGELOG.md is still not grouped with another (nothing else known); run `cargo test -p athena-core plan`.
criteria.evidence: The same test asserts that "same" (crates/a/src/lib.rs plus shared files) is in a different group from "one". It also asserts that "only" and "only2" (CHANGELOG.md only) are each alone in a group: `plan.groups[...] == ["only"]`. The existing test `two_items_naming_the_same_path_are_in_different_groups...` also still passes. All tests passed.

criteria.criterion: cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets pass, and cargo fmt --check is clean.
criteria.evidence: fmt printed nothing. clippy finished with no warnings. Every test binary in the full suite reported ok with 0 failures; some tests are ignored, as they are at base.

criteria.criterion: The shared append-only list (CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md, README.md) is one named constant in plan.rs with a doc comment citing parallel-jobs.md section 9, and the module docs describe the exception.
criteria.evidence: `const SHARED_APPEND_ONLY: [&str; 3] = ["CHANGELOG.md", "docs/decisions.md", "README.md"];` has a doc comment that cites `docs/design/parallel-jobs.md` section 9. The "Parallel groups" bullet of the module docs describes the exception, the behaviour of entries that touch only shared files, and that the landing check is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: The change stays within plan grouping; the docs say landing-check authority for conflicting shared-file edits is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: The only code change is in plan.rs: `grouping_paths` and `disjoint`, plus test fixtures. Two fixtures that used README.md as a stand-in non-shared path were switched to docs/a.md and docs/b.md. The module docs, parallel-jobs.md section 9 ('This changes grouping only; the landing check (rule 4) remains the authority'), D106 and CHANGELOG all say the landing check is unchanged.

findings.summary: Section 9 rule 3 (the pool should not run two jobs that name the same append-only file at once) now pulls against plan grouping, and the docs only say the rules are 'unchanged'.
findings.evidence: Rule 3 says jobs that name the same append-only file are serialized. After this change, plan groups deliberately contain items that share CHANGELOG.md, and the drain runs one group at once. The accepted reading treats rule 3 as a separate pool mechanism, which I did not find built (the table calls it a 'Hint'). A sentence saying the drain will now run shared-file writers at the same time, and the landing check catches the collision, would make this explicit. D106 'Tradeoff' does say this.

findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs is on the expected deliverables list but was not changed.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` lists only 4 files. The README.md paths in drain.rs are landing outputs (lines 156-158), not grouping inputs, so no change was needed there. No criterion requires a CLI-level test.

summary: The change does what was asked. `plan.rs` now leaves the shared append-only files (CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md, README.md, held in the named constant `SHARED_APPEND_ONLY`) out of the `disjoint` overlap test, so items that clash only on those files can share a parallel group. Items that touch the same code file stay apart, and an item that touches only shared files is still never grouped. A new unit test covers all three cases and would fail without the fix. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core plan`, the full `cargo test --locked`, clippy with -D warnings, and `cargo fmt --check` here; all passed. The module docs, parallel-jobs.md section 9, D106 and CHANGELOG all say the change affects grouping only and the landing check is unchanged. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. One minor finding: the new section 9 paragraph could say outright that grouped items may now write a shared file at the same time, which pulls against rule 3's serialization idea. The verdict is pass.
